apis.api_name: Reckon One Get Invoice API
apis.description:
Get a particular invoice.

`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/invoices/b696b9f5-e1e7-41f1-9f44-fa047e5e9ad2`

---

Get just the required fields, e.g. id and total amount. Find out more about [selecting](https://help.reckon.com/article/h9sxz6smwn-reckon-one-api-v2-selecting).

`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/invoices/b696b9f5-e1e7-41f1-9f44-fa047e5e9ad2?select=id,totalAmount`

---

Get an invoice as a PDF using a query string parameter.
    
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/invoices/b696b9f5-e1e7-41f1-9f44-fa047e5e9ad2?format=pdf`

---

Get an invoice as a PDF using a header instead of the query string parameter : `Accept: application/pdf`.

`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/invoices/b696b9f5-e1e7-41f1-9f44-fa047e5e9ad2`
apis.instructions: GET /{bookId}/invoices/{invoiceId}, sending an OAuth 2.0 bearer token and the API subscription key on every call. format is optional.
apis.authentication_details: OAuth 2.0 (authorization code) bearer token in the Authorization header plus an Azure API Management subscription key on every call, per Reckon's help centre (Reckon API authorisation services; Reckon One API v2 overview). The OpenAPI document itself declares no security scheme.

FR Flux 2 (FNFE) UBL overlay (profile ubl-flux2)
AFNOR EXTENDED-CTC-FR FNFE RFE 1.4.0.04 (profile ubl-extended-ctc-fr)

A key for the staging host is issued by entering a business e-mail address in the provider's SmartDocFlow testing tool (https://demo-api.staging.smartdocflow.com/), which e-mails it. apis.api_name: ESS SmartDocFlow Validate PINT A-NZ Invoice API
apis.official_api_name: Validate a Peppol PINT A-NZ invoice (Invoice root) against the UBL XSD and the PINT rule packs.
apis.description: Runs the Peppol PINT Australia / New Zealand compliance checks on a UBL invoice whose root element is Invoice (including one with credit-note type code 381), sent base64-encoded in content. Three checks run in order: the UBL 2.1 Invoice XSD, the PINT shared rules (170 asserts) and the A-NZ jurisdiction-aligned rules (74 asserts). The pack (billing or selfbilling) is detected from cbc:CustomizationID or declared in pack; checks may be limited to a subset. Every assert is fatal: the call returns 200 only when every check passes, otherwise each failing check with the OpenPeppol rule ids and messages.
apis.instructions: POST JSON {filename, content (the UBL XML in base64), pack: "billing"} to /peppol/aunz/validate/ubl with the x-api-key header. The key is issued through the SmartDocFlow web tool. Use /peppol/aunz/validate/ubl-creditnote for a credit note.
business_rules: Peppol PINT A-NZ Billing 1.1.3 (urn:peppol:pint:billing-1@aunz-1)
Peppol PINT A-NZ Self-billing 1.1.3 (urn:peppol:pint:selfbilling-1@aunz-1)
OASIS UBL 2.1 Invoice XSD
apis.authentication_details: API key in the x-api-key header. A key for the staging host is issued by entering a business e-mail address in the provider's SmartDocFlow testing tool (https://demo-api.staging.smartdocflow.com/), which e-mails it. Staging host xml.staging.smartdocflow.com/v1; the document also lists the production host xml.smartdocflow.com/v1.

apis.description: Returns the generated file as a raw binary body by default. apis.api_name: Attestwire API validateInvoice
apis.description:
Counts as one document against your monthly allowance. A response with `valid: false` is a successful call — it still costs a document. Findings come back in three arrays by severity: `errors` (fatal, the only ones that set `valid: false`), `warnings`, and `information` (advisory).

TWO WAYS TO SEND AN INVOICE, chosen by `content-type`.

`application/json` — our `InvoiceInput` model. Unchanged.

`application/xml` or `text/xml` — an **invoice document you already have**. We read it into the same invoice model and run the same rules, and the response adds `syntax` (which reader ran), `customizationId` (BT-24), `profileId` (BT-23), `unmapped` (everything in the file that did not reach the model) and `source`.

The reader takes **both EN 16931 syntaxes and both document types**: a UBL 2.1 `Invoice`, a UBL 2.1 `CreditNote`, and a UN/CEFACT CII `CrossIndustryInvoice`, which is one document for invoices and credit notes alike. Send the file as it is — there is no parameter for the syntax and none for the document type, because the root element decides both and the response reports what was read.

**It is not a PDF reader.** Factur-X and ZUGFeRD are CII XML inside a PDF/A-3 container; only the XML inside can be read here, so extract it and send that. A PDF, a `ubl:DebitNote`, or any other root element is refused with `415`.

Reading a file is a **pre-flight, not an authority**. We validate the model we read, not the XML a receiver judges, so rules that constrain the document itself (BR-01, BR-DE-13, BR-DE-21 on BT-24) do not run and a document that passes here can still be rejected by KoSIT or by a receiving platform.

METERING: an XML request costs one document once the file has been read and judged — `valid: true` and `valid: false` cost the same, exactly as on the JSON path. A file that cannot be read at all (`400`, `413`, `415`) never reaches the rules and costs nothing; those responses carry the unchanged `X-RateLimit-*` set so you can see the allowance did not move.
apis.instructions: POST InvoiceInput JSON or supported XML to /v1/validate; read valid and the returned findings.
business_rules: HTTP 200 can contain an invalid verdict. Fatal errors make valid false; warnings alone do not.
XML input is read into an invoice model; document-level rules BR-01, BR-DE-13 and BR-DE-21 on BT-24 do not run. A pre-flight pass is not recipient or KoSIT acceptance.
apis.authentication_details: Send the API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>.

apis.api_name: Attestwire API generateInvoice
apis.description:
Validates first: a fatal rule failure returns 422 with the same teaching errors as /v1/validate, and does not consume a document. Supported profiles in this build: en16931, xrechnung-ubl, peppol-bis-3, xrechnung-cii, facturx-en16931.

THE PROFILE CHOOSES THE SYNTAX. xrechnung-cii and facturx-en16931 come back as UN/CEFACT CII; every other profile comes back as UBL 2.1. The JSON response says which in its `syntax` field.

**CII output is XML, not a PDF.** Factur-X and ZUGFeRD files are CII XML inside a PDF/A-3 container. This endpoint returns the XML. It does not build the container, does not attach the XML as `factur-x.xml` and does not set `/AFRelationship`, so a `facturx-en16931` response is the payload and not a Factur-X document. Pass it to a Factur-X packaging library if you need the file.

**Output verification is not uniform, and is never per-request.** The generator's `xrechnung-cii` fixture documents are run through the official KoSIT validator on release and accepted. The `facturx-en16931` fixtures are not: that profile's BT-24 is the core EN 16931 one, which matches no XRechnung scenario, so KoSIT answers "no scenario matched" instead of a verdict, and an absence of a verdict is not a pass. Neither case says anything about YOUR document: this endpoint does not send anything to KoSIT.

The JSON envelope carries `provenance`: the engine version and rule set that cleared this document. `?format=xml` returns the bytes alone and therefore carries none — an XML document has nowhere to put it, and this API does not write its own metadata into a customer's tax document. Read GET /v1/versions if you need it for a raw-XML pipeline.
apis.instructions: POST InvoiceInput JSON to /v1/generate; add format=xml for raw XML instead of the default JSON envelope.
business_rules: Generation runs validation first; fatal failures return 422. Use a profile listed in the generation matrix.
apis.authentication_details: Send the API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>.

pack.description:
Which PINT A-NZ specialisation to validate against.

Omit it and the server detects the pack from the document's
`cbc:CustomizationID` (the same `starts-with` test the packs'
own identity rules use); `details.pack_source` then reads
`"detected"`.

Supply it and it is an **assertion that wins**: the declared
pack runs even if the document identifies as the other one —
which is what a Peppol access point would report — and the
response adds `details.pack_mismatch` naming both sides so
nobody has to decode the identity rule ids by hand.

Detection is only attempted when a Schematron check is
requested. With `checks: ["xsd"]` no pack is needed and
`details.pack_source` is `"not_required"`.

A document with no recognisable `cbc:CustomizationID` and no
`pack` is rejected with `400` / `PACK_REQUIRED` rather than
guessed at — guessing produces a wall of identity failures
that hides the real problem.

checks.description:
Which checks to run. Omit for all three. Set semantics: the
server runs the requested checks in the canonical order
`xsd` → `pint-shared` → `pint-aligned` whatever order they
were sent in, and echoes the effective list in
`details.checks`, so a partial run is explicit in the
response. An empty list, or any unrecognised id, is `400` /
`CHECK_UNKNOWN`.

meaning later is a non-breaking change.

- `PACK_REQUIRED` — a Schematron check was requested, the

- `FIELD_RESERVED` — the request carried a reserved field

allOf.description:
States for an issued invoice:
 * `new` - The initial status of an invoice.
 * `sending` - The invoice is currently being transmitted (queued for delivery).
 * `sent` - The invoice has been sent successfully.
 * `read` - A read notification has been received from the recipient (e.g. via PEPPOL network).
 * `accepted` - The invoice has been accepted by the recipient or manually marked as accepted.
 * `registered` - A registered notification has been received from a tax authority or manually marked as registered.
 * `refused` - A refused notification has been received or the invoice was manually marked as refused.
 * `received` - Used in integration context to indicate the document was received by the recipient system.
 * `allegedly_paid` - The receiver has indicated that payment of the invoice has been ordered, but payment is not yet confirmed.
 * `paid` - The invoice has been fully paid.
 * `annulled` - The invoice has been voided or cancelled (e.g. via a C4 annulment notification).
 * `expired` - The invoice has passed its due date or validity period without being acted upon.
 * `issued` - The invoice has been formally issued in the tax system (C1 corner state tracking).
 * `error` - An error occurred while sending or processing the invoice.
 * `closed` - Final state indicating the invoice lifecycle is complete.

States for a received invoice:
 * `performing_ocr` - The system is extracting text from the received invoice file using OCR.
 * `ocr_failed` - OCR processing failed and the file could not be read or processed.
 * `new` - The initial status of a received invoice (or after successful OCR processing).
 * `accepted` - The invoice has been marked as accepted.
 * `refused` - The invoice has been marked as refused.
 * `annotated` - The invoice has been marked with an accounting annotation.
 * `billed` - The invoice has been recorded as billed for accounting purposes.
 * `payment_processed` - Payment processing for the invoice has been completed.
 * `paid` - The invoice has been fully paid.
 * `invalid` - The invoice failed validation during import or reception.
 * `error` - An error occurred while processing the invoice.

States for an issued simplified invoice:
 * `new` - The initial status of an invoice.
 * `sending` - The invoice is currently being transmitted (queued for delivery).
 * `sent` - The invoice has been sent successfully.
 * `paid` - The invoice has been paid or manually marked as paid.
 * `downloaded` - The invoice has been downloaded by the recipient or manually marked as downloaded.
 * `accepted` - The invoice has been marked as accepted.
 * `refused` - When the invoice is marked as refused.
 * `registered` - When a registered notification has been received or manually marked as registered.
 * `closed` - Final state indicating the invoice lifecycle is complete.

States for an issued self-invoice:
 * `new` - The initial status of an invoice.
 * `sending` - The invoice is currently being transmitted (queued for delivery).
 * `sent` - The invoice has been sent successfully.
 * `accepted` - The invoice has been marked as accepted.
 * `registered` - A registered notification has been received or manually marked as registered.
 * `allegedly_paid` - The receiver has indicated that payment has been ordered, but payment is not yet confirmed.
 * `payment_processed` - Payment processing for the invoice has been completed.
 * `paid` - The invoice has been fully paid.
 * `closed` - Final state indicating the invoice lifecycle is complete.

See [Sending a Message with STO](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/sending-messages/send-sto) for details. *Please note that STO is only available on certain plans. When set to 'yes', requires the message to be sent only over a TLS connection to the Email Service Provider. If TLS cannot be established, the message will not be delivered. When set to 'no' (default), Mailgun attempts TLS but falls back to plaintext SMTP if needed.

Specify a second domain key to sign the email with. The value is formatted as `signing_domain/selector`, e.g. `example.com/s1`. Specify an alias of the domain key specified in `o:secondary-dkim`. Also formatted as `public_signing_domain/selector`. `o:secondary-dkim` option must also be provided. Note: We will perform a DNS check prior to signing the message to ensure the public keys matches the secondary DKIM.

Which checks to run. Omit for all three. Set semantics: the
server runs the requested checks in the canonical order
`xsd` → `pint-shared` → `pint-aligned` whatever order they
were sent in, and echoes the effective list in
`details.checks`, so a partial run is explicit in the
response. An empty list, or any unrecognised id, is `400` /
`CHECK_UNKNOWN`.

Supply it and it is an **assertion that wins**: the declared
pack runs even if the document identifies as the other one —
which is what a Peppol access point would report — and the
response adds `details.pack_mismatch` naming both sides so
nobody has to decode the identity rule ids by hand.

Detection is only attempted when a Schematron check is

`details.pack_source` is `"not_required"`.

guessed at — guessing produces a wall of identity failures

Controls how VAT totals are rounded for this invoice, overriding the
account-level setting of the same name.

- `true` — taxes are computed per line (each line rounded, then summed).
- `false` — taxes are computed per invoice (taxable base summed per rate, then rounded once).
- omitted / `null` — inherit the account's `apply_taxes_per_line` setting.

The override is honoured only for premium accounts. Public administrations
that recompute totals may reject an invoice whose rounding mode doesn't
match theirs; use this field to align per invoice.

schema.title: Document Type Code
schema.description:
An internal identifier that is unique to each **Document Type** within B2Brouter.
You can get all valid document type codes using the **Document Types** endpoint in Code lists section (`/document_types`).

api_parameter.description:
Internal identifier that specifies the **Document Type** used for the **contact party** of the invoice within B2Brouter. This code determines the format in which the document is exchanged with the contact entity.

- If the contact already exists, this value will **overwrite** the existing `document_type_code`.
- If the parameter is **not provided**, the system assigns the `document_type_code` based on the following priority:

  1. If the contact already exists, its current `document_type_code` is used.
  2. If the contact does not exist:
     - If the contact is found in the **B2Brouter directory**, the code defined there is used.
     - Otherwise, the **default document type** defined in the account settings is applied.

Valid document type codes can be retrieved from the **Document Types** endpoint in the **Code Lists** section:  
`/document_types`

If the specified `document_type_code` is **invalid** or **incompatible** with the selected `transport_type_code`, the system will apply the **default** `transport_type_code` and `document_type_code`.

api_parameter.name: issue_after_import

schema.description:
Indicates whether the invoice should be issued synchronously after creation/import, without going through the transport send flow.

When set to `true` and the invoice passes validations:
  * The invoice transitions to `state=issued` (c1 corner) inline.
  * If the account has a `before_send` tax report setting enabled with `auto_generate` on and the invoice qualifies, the tax report is generated inline and exposed via `tax_report_ids`. When `auto_generate` is off the invoice is still issued but no report is created, consistent with the send flow — those reports are managed through the Tax Reports API.
  * Authorities that report after sending (for example SII or SDI) are not triggered by issuing; their reports are created when the invoice is sent or marked as sent.
  * No background send job is enqueued; the transport-level state (c2) remains untouched.
  * While in `state=issued` the invoice becomes read-only: it cannot be updated, deleted, or reverted to `new` until it is sent or downloaded.

If both `send_after_import` and `issue_after_import` are `true`, `send_after_import` wins (sending already issues the invoice). Ignored for non-invoice documents.

schema.description:
Indicates whether the invoice should be automatically processed after creation/import.

When set to `true` and the invoice passes validations:
  * For sending transports (non-`download`), the invoice is queued to be sent asynchronously.
  * For `download` transport, the invoice is not sent. Instead, if tax report generation is enabled and required for this invoice, the invoice will be issued and the tax report generated 
    (invoice ends in `state=issued` and exposes `tax_report_ids`). Otherwise, the invoice may end in `state=error`.

**Note:** This option is incompatible with the custom signature configuration.
